datasets.name: Landslide inventory of Eastern Iburi, Hokkaido, Japan
datasets.verbatim: Our primary source of the landslide inventory is the map produced by Zhang et al. (2019) and applied in studies like (Ghorbanzadeh et al., 2021).

datasets.name: Sentinel-2A imagery (pre- and post-landslide)
datasets.verbatim: The cloud-free available pre- (23.05.2016) and post- (06.08.2019) landslide event Sentinel-2 images are downloaded, and atmospheric corrections are made using the useful Sen2Cor plugin in the SNAP software developed by the European Space Agency (ESA).

datasets.name: JAXA ALOS Digital Elevation Model (DEM)
datasets.verbatim: The training and testing datasets include optical satellite imagery from Sentinel-2 and the digital elevation model from the Japanese aerospace exploration agency sensor of JAXA ALOS.

methods.name: Integrated ResU-Net and rule-based OBIA
methods.summary: The method integrates a ResU-Net deep learning model for generating landslide probability maps with a rule-based Object-Based Image Analysis (OBIA) approach. The OBIA stage uses spectral, spatial, and contextual features (including land cover and image difference indices) to refine the ResU-Net probability outputs through predefined threshold-based rulesets to delineate landslide boundaries.
methods.source: Omid Ghorbanzadeh, Khalil Gholamnia & Pedram Ghamisi
methods.verbatim: This study evaluates a rule-based object-based image analysis (OBIA) approach built on probabilities resulting from the ResU-Net model for landslide detection.

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory and other input datasets are mentioned but not linked, and the custom code for the ResU-Net and OBIA method is not provided or linked.
